page.title: Ironman Marbella 2041: Recovery Day on a Boat Charter

data.meta_description: Recharge after Ironman Marbella 2041 with a recovery boat charter in Puerto Banús. Relax on our fleet, enjoy included drinks & snacks, and soothe sore muscles on the Mediterranean.
data.summary: Post-race recovery meets luxury on a boat charter from Puerto Banús after Ironman Marbella 2041. Choose from our fleet, enjoy included refreshments, and let the sea work its magic.
key_facts: Ironman Marbella 2041 takes place on 26 April 2041.

faq.q: How close is Puerto Banús to the Ironman Marbella 2041 finish line?
faq.a: Puerto Banús is roughly 4 km (a 10-minute drive) from the Marbella town-centre finish area. Most athletes and supporters head straight to the port for post-race celebrations or recovery charters. We meet you at the dock – no extra transfers needed.

faq.q: Can I charter a boat for just a few hours after the race?
faq.a: Absolutely. Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) start at €749 for 2 hours. That’s enough time to cruise the coast, enjoy a drink, and take a gentle swim. For longer recovery, the 8-hour option (€2,299) gives you a full day on the water.

faq.q: What’s included in the charter price?
faq.a: Every booking includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden costs – just show up and relax.

faq.q: Is the Mangusta 80 suitable for a recovery day?
faq.a: Yes. The Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) offers spacious deck areas, sun loungers, and a shaded saloon. Its minimum 4-hour charter (€4,719) includes a free jet ski – perfect if you want a gentle ride or some active recovery. The boat’s stability makes it ideal for post-race relaxation.

faq.q: What’s the best time to charter after the Ironman?
faq.a: The race typically finishes by mid-afternoon. We recommend a late-afternoon charter (e.g., 16:00–18:00) to catch the golden hour. The sea is calm, the sun is lower, and the temperature is pleasant. April averages 16°C water temperature – refreshing but not cold.

faq.q: Can I bring my own recovery gear (foam rollers, massage tools)?
faq.a: Yes, you’re welcome to bring small recovery items. Our boats have ample deck space and cabins for changing. Just keep in mind that space is shared with other passengers (up to 12 on larger boats). We recommend a small bag.

faq.q: Do you offer catering for post-race nutrition?
faq.a: Our standard charter includes light snacks (nuts, crisps, fruit) and drinks. For a more substantial recovery meal, we can arrange a catered platter (order via WhatsApp at least 48 hours in advance). Options include sandwiches, salads, and protein boxes.

faq.q: How do I book a recovery charter for Ironman Marbella 2041?
faq.a: Contact us via WhatsApp (link on our website) with your preferred boat, date, and time. We’ll confirm availability and send a secure payment link. Early booking is recommended – charters sell out quickly on race weekend.

data.body_html:
Completing Ironman Marbella 2041 is a monumental achievement. After 3.8 km of swimming, 180 km of cycling, and a full marathon, your body deserves more than a protein shake and a cold shower. A recovery boat charter on the Mediterranean is the ultimate way to soothe sore muscles, rehydrate in style, and celebrate with your support crew. Departing from Puerto Banús, our fleet offers everything from a quick 2-hour sunset cruise to a full-day luxury escape – all with included drinks, snacks, and a licensed skipper. Here’s how to plan your perfect post-race recovery day.

Why a Boat Charter Is Ideal for Ironman Recovery

Active recovery – light movement, gentle swimming, and mental relaxation – speeds up muscle repair without stressing your body. A boat charter provides all three: the gentle rocking of the sea, a cool dip in 16°C April water, and panoramic views of the Costa del Sol. Plus, you avoid the crowds of Marbella’s beach clubs. Our charters include everything you need: skipper, fuel, drinks, and snacks. No planning, no stress – just show up and float.

All boats depart from Puerto Banús. For pricing on other models (e.g., Pershing 46, Fairline Targa, Lagoon 380), contact us via WhatsApp.

Recommended Recovery Itinerary (4-Hour Charter)

  • 15:30 – Meet at Puerto Banús dock. Your skipper welcomes you with chilled water and soft drinks.
  • 16:00 – Depart west towards Cabopino. Gentle cruise at 8–10 knots – no rocking.
  • 16:30 – Anchor at Cala del Faro for a 15-minute swim in calm, clear water.
  • 17:00 – Light snacks (nuts, fruit, crisps) and a glass of cava or beer.
  • 17:30 – Cruise back east past the Golden Mile, spotting La Concha mountain.
  • 18:30 – Return to Puerto Banús. You’re recharged, relaxed, and ready for dinner.

What’s Included in Every Charter

  • Licensed English-speaking skipper
  • Fuel for the entire charter
  • Water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava
  • Light snacks (fruit, crisps, nuts)
  • Insurance and safety equipment
  • Spanish IVA (21%) – no surprise taxes

You don’t need to bring anything except swimwear, sunscreen, and a towel. We provide everything else.

Practical Tips for Race Day

  • Book early – April is a popular month; charters fill up quickly on Ironman weekend.
  • Arrive 15 minutes early – parking near Puerto Banús can be busy. Use the underground car park at the port.
  • Hydrate on board – we provide unlimited water, but bring your own electrolyte tabs if you prefer.
  • Consider a longer charter – if you’re with family or supporters, the 8-hour option (€2,299 on Tier A boats) gives you time to visit Estepona or Sotogrande.
